Can you put together a timeline and ownership matrix? Our security team wants to know the earliest possible date we can go live with enforced IP allowlisting without causing downtime for our users.

Also: we will attach our SAML metadata and our preferred IP ranges once we confirm the rollout date.

Olivia

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear ask. Below is a proposed timeline and a short checklist by owner. I’ve attached a first-draft implementation timeline (PDF) and a privilege mapping CSV for reference.

Summary timeline (target):
- Week of May 24: Exchange SAML metadata + test IdP SSO against staging tenant
- May 25–26: SCIM attribute mapping review and staging provisioning test (delta/full cycle)
- May 27 (maintenance window): IP allowlist enforcement in staging; service account provisioning + token rotation policy applied to staging accounts
- Week of May 31: Production cutover with staged IP whitelist enforcement and monitoring rollback policy

Owner breakdown:
- SAML metadata & SSO test: Finova IdP (Olivia) + Jasmine (CS)
- SCIM attribute map & provisioning: Finova IT + Dev (Infra)
- IP allowlist cutover: Finova infra + Laura (Customer Ops) + Ben (SE) for traffic validation
- Service accounts & token rotation: Dev (Infra) to apply naming and rotation policy; Jasmine to confirm org-level policy enforcement

Questions for you before we lock dates:
1) Do you have a preferred SAML metadata file (we’ll accept XML) and the Signing cert?
2) What SCIM scope do you need: just user + group sync, or do you plan to provision role assignments as SCIM attributes?
3) Confirm your preferred IP CIDR blocks for the allowlist test window (we’ll need both staging and prod ranges if they differ).

If those answers are ready today we can lock the May 24–31 plan. Ben and Dev — looping you in to confirm SE/infra questions below (service-account patterns + SCIM rate limits).

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Privileged Boundaries & Network Whitelist: Implementation Timeline for Finova

Adding a couple of implementation notes from the SE side:

- Service accounts: recommend per-environment service accounts (finova-prod-infer, finova-staging-infer) with role scoping via our RBAC groups. Token lifetime: rotate every 90 days; immediate revocation support if a key compromise is suspected. Attached is a sample privilege map (redwood_privilege-map-v1.csv).
- SCIM provisioning: we support incremental provisioning (PATCH/PUT) and full sync. For minimal disruption, plan for delta provisioning in staging first. Note: SCIM rate limits are 200 requests/min by default; we can request a temporary bump for initial sync if you need it.
- IP allowlist cutover strategy: recommend a two-step approach — first add Redwood egress IPs to the allowlist (no enforcement), monitor for 48 hours, then flip enforcement. This avoids breaking existing sessions.

Happy to jump on a quick 30-min call with Finova infra to walk through the service-account naming and token lifecycle.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Privileged Boundaries & Network Whitelist: Implementation Timeline for Finova

Quick technical checklist from infra:

- SAML: We support SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows. For SAML metadata we need: entityID, ACS URL (we’ll provide staging + prod), and signing cert. Test in staging with our SP metadata first.
- SCIM mapping: prefer the following attributes to map from Finova IdP: userName, givenName, familyName, mail, groups. If you need to sync role assignments, include an attribute named 'x-redwood-role' in your SCIM payload; we'll map it to RBAC groups.
- SCIM provisioning window: schedule full initial sync during low activity (overnight). Delta syncs can run every 5 minutes; note the 200 rpm default.
- IP allowlist specifics: send us the CIDR ranges for both staging and prod. We will provide a maintenance page and a rollback playbook; during enforcement flip we will keep an emergency bypass account for 15 minutes in case of issues.
- Service accounts: we will create service accounts with least privilege and attach a managed key that supports rotation. Token revocation is immediate via the console or API.

Operational links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-finova-plan (staging playbooks and runbooks)

I can be available for the May 25 SCIM test slot between 08:00–12:00 PT.

—Dev
